Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

vellumplot (development version)

vellumplot 0.22.1

Bug fixes

  • Edges stop at the rim of a mark_node_pie() pie, as they do at a mark_nodes() marker (VP-130). They used to run to the pie’s centre, so an arrowhead into a pie was hidden under it, and parallel or reciprocal edges between pies were drawn on top of each other. A vertex with both a marker and a pie caps at the larger of the two.

Documentation

  • The inset() examples and the composition article give their insets a larger box (VP-131). Since align_to = "panel" became the default (VP-127) the fractions are of the panel, and the old boxes left the histogram inset cramped.

vellumplot 0.22.0

Breaking changes

  • A bare name in a mark argument that is not a column of the layer’s data and holds a single value is now a setting, not a mapping (VP-126). ink <- "#f4eee0"; mark_ridgeline(color = ink) draws in that colour, like color = "#f4eee0"; it used to map the value, adding a one-entry legend and a default colour. A non-column name holding one value per row still maps, and a column still wins over a variable of the same name. I(x) forces a setting and .env$x forces a mapping (with the legend titled x). The check runs at draw time against the layer’s own data (else the plot’s), and covers the scaled aesthetics (color, fill, size, shape, alpha, linewidth, linetype, pattern, edge_*); a spec exported with as_spec() / spec_to_json() / spec_to_vegalite() carries the value. See “Mappings and settings” in ?mark_point.

  • inset() honours align_to (VP-127). The default "panel" now takes left / bottom / right / top as fractions of the base plot’s panel area (all panels of a faceted plot), "plot" of the plot without its title, subtitle and caption, and "full" of the whole base cell, as patchwork’s inset_element() does. Insets used to be placed in the whole base cell whatever align_to said, so an existing inset moves into the panel and gets smaller; pass align_to = "full" to keep the old placement. A composition of several plots still places its insets in the whole figure.

  • theme_void() has no plot margin, matching ggplot2 (VP-128): a void plot now fills its box edge to edge, where it kept the 5.5 mm plot.margin of theme_gray(). Maps, locator insets and other void plots grow by that margin; add theme(plot.margin = c(5.5, 5.5, 5.5, 5.5)) for the old look.

New features

  • mark_node_pie() wedge colours get a legend (VP-123): the cols are the categories of the fill scale, so the legend names them (untitled unless labs(fill =) gives a title) and scale_fill_manual() / scale_fill_brewer() recolour the wedges; colours given with fill = become the scale’s values. size can be mapped (size = total), drawn through the size scale with a size legend of neutral grey discs.

Bug fixes

  • mark_node_text(repel = TRUE) leader lines stop at the rim of the node glyph under the label (a mark_nodes() marker or a mark_node_pie() pie, plus the small gap edges leave) instead of running over it to the vertex centre, which made a single-colour pie look as if it had a radial line (VP-129). Static renders and widget payloads both carry the trimmed leader.

  • mark_node_pie() draws a node made of a single category as a whole disc (or ring, for a donut) instead of a 360-degree wedge, whose radial edges showed a seam from the centre to the rim (VP-122).

  • spec_to_vegalite() exports scale: {zero: false} on a continuous x or y scale whose data leaves zero out, so the Vega-Lite chart frames the data as vellumplot does instead of stretching the axis to zero (VP-124). A layer’s tooltip = now exports as Vega-Lite’s tooltip channel (a plot with any interactivity used to fail to export), and spec_from_vegalite() imports the tooltip channel (one field, an array of fields, or true) into the layer’s tooltip instead of dropping it.

  • guide_bivariate() sizes its swatches so the break labels on the x edge no longer run into each other (VP-125). The automatic size fitted the widest label, but the first label starts at its edge rather than centring on it, so it could reach the second. The swatch now fits each pair of neighbouring labels plus a 1 mm gap.

  • A cartesian panel’s scale metadata now says which gridlines the panel draws along each axis (grid = list(major, minor), from the theme’s panel.grid.major.* / panel.grid.minor.*), so a widget re-ticking the axes draws the same set (VW-66). In a composition, a cell themed with panel.grid = element_blank() used to get gridlines back in the widget.

  • mark_rule() draws under coord_polar() and coord_radial() (VP-121), where the layer used to vanish without a warning. An intercept on the radius aesthetic is a circle (an arc over a partial coord_radial(end =) sweep) and one on the angle aesthetic a spoke from the inner to the outer radius.

  • An aligned composition (concat(), hconcat(), vconcat()) draws each sub-plot’s own labs(title, subtitle, caption, tag) (VP-119). The shared grid reserved their rows but drew nothing into them, leaving a blank band above the panel. Each band spans its own cell and lines up with the other cells of its row.

  • An element set with theme() is drawn even when its parent is blank, as in ggplot2: theme_void() |> theme(axis.text.x = element_text()) now draws the x axis labels, which a blank axis.text used to swallow. The element takes its unset properties from its nearest non-blank ancestor. A preset’s own elements still follow a blank parent, so theme_classic() and theme_void() draw no minor gridlines.

  • animate() no longer suggests a data_id for mark_ridgeline() and mark_violin() layers. Each ridge or violin is one outline per group, so its rows are never paired by order; the hint fired whenever the groups had different numbers of rows in different states.

  • A secondary axis on a log scale gets log breaks: scale_x_continuous(trans = "log10", sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . * 2.2)) ticks the secondary axis at powers of ten, as in ggplot2, where it used linear breaks that left one or two crowded labels at the top of the range. The secondary’s default breaks now come from the primary scale’s transform, and the labels are placed through a lookup grid spaced evenly along the axis.

  • A fixed-aspect plot (coord_fixed(), coord_sf(), coord_polar(), theme(aspect.ratio =)) placed with inset() or vellum::scene_inset() fits its box (VP-120). It kept the whole box and letterboxed its panel inside, so a small locator map sat shrunk in the middle of a mostly empty frame. inset() now shrinks the box to the plot’s shape, keeping the side nearest the edge the box sits on, and an aspect-locked plot’s scene tells vellum::scene_inset() its shape (needs vellum with fit =). inset() also gains shadow = for a soft drop shadow, and names each inset’s viewport "inset-<k>".

vellumplot 0.21.1

Bug fixes

  • Point legend keys of a layer with a tiny constant size are no smaller than a readable minimum (VP-118): theme(legend.key.point.min =), a radius in mm, defaulting to 1 (an unsized point’s radius). Since VP-113 (0.21.0) a plot of small points keyed its colour, shape, merged and alpha legends at the points’ size, too small to read. The cap at half the key side stays; a size legend keeps its mapped sizes, an override.aes size is kept as given, and SVG icon keys keep the key size.

vellumplot 0.21.0

Bug fixes

  • Point legend keys take a point layer’s constant size (VP-113): mark_point(shape = g, size = 1) keys its shapes at the points’ size (with R’s per-shape size factors), not at the larger default key size. Colour and alpha keys of a point layer do the same. A size larger than the key keeps to the key; a size legend keeps its mapped sizes. SVG icon keys keep the key size, as an icon’s size scales it far beyond a point’s.

  • Line-type, line-width and line-only merged legend keys draw in their layer’s colour, its default black (the theme’s ink) unless the layer sets a constant color, and alpha keys of a point or line layer likewise (VP-114). They were grey35 and grey20.

  • On a narrow date axis the sparser break candidates keep the short labels of the denser ones where those stay distinct (VP-116): six-monthly breaks read “Jan Jul”, not pretty()’s “2023-01 2023-07”, which were wider than the “Jan Apr Jul” that did not fit.

  • ggplot2’s point shapes 8 and 11 draw as R draws them (VP-115): 8 is an asterisk (a plus over a cross, at the sizes of 3 and 4) and 11 two overlaid triangles with R’s proportions, both stroke-only, in the plot and in the legend keys. Both drew as an open star.

  • ggplot2’s point shapes 7, 9, 10, 12, 13 and 14 draw both of their glyphs (a square with a cross, a diamond with a plus, a circle with a plus, a square with a plus, a circle with a cross, a square with a triangle), as R does; they drew as the plain open square, diamond or circle.

  • mark_crossbar(width =) is in data units, as mark_errorbar(width =) and mark_bar(width =) are and as in ggplot2’s geom_crossbar() (VP-105). It was a fraction of the band, so on a continuous x a box could be many times too wide. The default is now 90% of the band, ggplot2’s default (it was 50%), so cross-bars line up with bars and error bars. Dodged cross-bars share the width among the groups, and the boxes train a continuous axis, so the outer boxes are not clipped.

  • mark_crossbar() draws its middle line 2.5 times as wide as the box outline, as ggplot2’s geom_crossbar() does; it drew both at one width, so the middle value did not stand out.

  • ggplot2’s solid point shapes 15-18 and 20 draw as in ggplot2 (VP-106). R draws 15-18 without an outline, so a 16 is slightly smaller than a 19, and 20 (the bullet) at 2/3 the size of 19; vellumplot drew them all outlined at full size. Legend keys draw them the same way. By name these are "circle bare" (and so on, no outline) and "circle small".

  • Colour and size legend keys draw a point layer’s constant shape whatever it is (VP-107): mark_point(shape = "square", color = g) keys its colours with squares, not circles. VP-103 did this only for open and bordered shapes.

  • Size and shape legend keys take a point layer’s constant colour: mark_point(size = hp, color = "red") keyed its sizes in grey.

  • Point legend keys default to the points’ own colour (VP-109): size, shape and merged size + shape keys of mark_point(size = hp) are black, as the points are and as ggplot2 keys them, where they were grey. A merged size + shape legend takes a constant color too, and a constant fill that colours solid points colours their keys.

  • Mapping shape to a variable or column of SVG paths warns (VP-112): it is a mapping like any other, so the levels cycle through the shape palette. The warning points to the literal string (or shape = !!path) for one icon and to scale_shape_identity() for each row’s own icon.

  • ggplot2’s point shape codes draw at R’s size for each symbol (VP-111). R’s graphics engine scales its symbols from the circle’s radius: triangles (2, 6, 17, 24, 25) are drawn about 1.56 times vellum’s triangle, so their area matches the circle’s; the open diamond (5, 9) is sqrt(2) and the bordered one (23) 1.25 times vellum’s diamond; the bordered square (22) is 0.89 of the open and solid squares (0, 15); and the plus (3) and cross (4) are sqrt(2) times vellum’s. vellumplot drew them all at one size, so pch 17 looked much smaller than in ggplot2. The plain marker names keep their sizes.

  • The date-break fit judges each pair of neighbouring labels by the mean of their two widths (VP-110). It required the widest label’s width between every pair, so a month axis was thinned by its widest month name even where narrower names sat side by side; a six-month axis now keeps monthly labels on a slightly narrower plot.

vellumplot 0.20.0

Bug fixes

  • mark_errorbar(width =) is in data units, as mark_bar(width =) is since VP-98 and as in ggplot2’s geom_errorbar() (VP-104). It was a fraction of the band, so on a continuous x the caps did not match the bars (width = 4 on an axis with a resolution of 10 drew caps 40 units wide). The default is now 90% of the band, ggplot2’s default and a default bar’s width (it was 50%), so error bars over bars span them. Dodged error bars share the width among the groups as dodged bars do, and the caps train a continuous axis, as bars’ edges do, so the outer caps are not clipped.

  • ggplot2’s numeric point shapes draw as in ggplot2 (VP-103). The open codes 0-14 draw only an outline in the point colour, the solid 15-20 fill with it, and the bordered 21-25 fill with fill inside a color outline (black by default; unfilled when no fill is given). Before, all three families drew the same solid marker, so scale_shape_manual(values = c(1, 0)) gave filled circles and squares. The variants are also available by name ("circle open", "square filled", …). Legend keys follow: shape keys, colour and size keys of a point layer with a constant open or bordered shape, merged keys and override.aes = list(shape = ). In vellumwidget the hollow fallback dots (VW-63) now pick these marks up.

  • A constant numeric shape (mark_point(shape = 1)) and numeric codes under scale_shape_identity() drew no points at all: the code was read as an SVG icon path. They now map to their marker, as scale_shape_manual() values do.

  • A date axis on which no pretty() breaks fit keeps the first and last break of the sparsest candidate with two in range, so the reader can still tell the scale (VP-102). VP-92’s fallback could leave a single label (a 20-year axis beside a wide legend showed only “2000”; it now shows “2000” and “2010”).

  • mark_bar(width =) is honoured (VP-98): it sets the bar width in data units, as in ggplot2’s geom_bar(), where it was ignored and bars stayed at 90% of the resolution. Dodged bars share it, and the continuous-x extent training (VP-90) now follows the drawn bars exactly, so a narrow or position_dodge(width =) layer pads the axis as ggplot2 does.

  • mark_tile() and mark_raster() on a continuous axis are no longer clipped at the ends (VP-99): the tiles’ edges (centre +/- half the width / height) train the x and y scales, as ggplot2 does, the tile version of VP-90. A constant mark_tile(width =, height =) is honoured too (it was ignored).

  • The discrete size and alpha scales (scale_size_discrete(), scale_size_ordinal(), scale_size_manual() and their scale_alpha_*() twins) gain drop = (VP-100), as VP-91 gave the colour, fill, shape and linetype scales: drop = FALSE keeps a factor level no row uses in the legend and the output range.

  • Date-break fitting (VP-92) reads guide_axis(angle =, n.dodge =) and measures the panel the way the layout does (VP-101). Rotated labels only need their line height between them, and labels staggered over n.dodge rows sit n.dodge breaks apart, so such an axis gets denser breaks. The axis length used to be estimated as 75% of the plot’s width. It now subtracts the plot margins, the legends, the other axis’s title and label gutter, the title/subtitle/caption bands (for a vertical axis) and the panel spacing, so a wide legend thins the date labels instead of letting them collide. The wanted gap between labels is now 1 mm (was 2 mm, which was calibrated against the rough estimate).

  • mark_edge_bundle()’s legend key is a line, drawn at the bundle’s default 0.3 opacity (VP-73). It was a square swatch at full opacity.

  • A flow-map trunk’s default tooltip names the destinations it carries (VP-74), e.g. “v1 → v3, v5, v8: 35”, or “v1 → v2, v3, v4 + 2 more: 90” past three, where it said “v1 → …: 35”.

vellumplot 0.19.0

New features

  • animate() gains start_pause, end_pause and rewind (VP-95), with gganimate’s semantics: hold the first / last frame for that many frames, and play back to the start; they come out of nframes. GIF, APNG and SVG files, anim_frame() and the animated widget’s scrubber all follow them.

  • anim_frame(filename, animation, frame) saves one frame of an animation as a PNG, SVG or PDF (VP-96), drawn exactly as in the animation (same frozen scales, tween and frame variables), so a poster matches its animation. The default frame is the one shown under reduced motion: the final frame of an animation that ends on its last state, else the first. Needs vellum’s new vl_render_frame().

  • mark_text() labels may use frame variables in an animation (VP-93): label = "{round(frame_time)}" (a constant, or a column of templates) is filled in on every frame, through vellum’s per-frame text, while the label moves as its mark. Repelled and rich-text labels are not templated.

  • animate() tells you, once, when marks without a data_id are matched by row order within groups whose size changes between states, and suggests a data_id (VP-87).

  • Frame variables in animation titles (VP-82): labs(title = "Year: {round(frame_time)}"), glue-style, as in gganimate. Available: frame, nframes, progress always; closest_state, previous_state, next_state, transitioning for transition_states(); frame_time for transition_time(); frame_along for transition_reveal(). Each {...} is an R expression evaluated per frame. The title, subtitle and caption update on every frame, not only at keyframes: each distinct string is shaped once and swapped into the tweened frame by vellum’s new per-frame text (needs vellum 0.13.0.9000). Data labels (mark_text()) are not templated. See Frame variables in ?animate.

  • animate() supports faceted plots (VP-84). Every panel of the whole data is drawn in every frame (a state with no rows for a panel leaves it empty instead of changing the layout, which would cut), the scales are frozen across frames as before, and a mark’s identity includes its panel, so a row whose facet value changes fades out of one panel and into the other rather than sliding across. Per-panel scales (scales = "free", "free_x", "free_y", or an independent resolve_scale()) are refused with a clear message, since frozen scales cannot honour them. transition_reveal() works with facets too.

  • anim_save() writes .apng as well as .png (both an animated PNG), and explains a video (.mp4, .webm, …) or .webp filename instead of a bare “must end in” error: there is no encoder for them, so it suggests saving an APNG/GIF and converting it (an ffmpeg or magick one-liner). render_plot() on an animation now says to use anim_save() (or to render the plot before animate() for a still) instead of a class error (VP-85).

  • transition_time() accepts Date and POSIXct times (VP-83). They run on their numeric value (segments weighted by the day/second gaps) and keep their class for {frame_time} (with the time zone) and in the cut warning’s state names.

Bug fixes

  • outline(), shadow() and glow(color =) on a multi-series line draw one underlay per series again (VP-97). The recoloured underlay dropped the colour mapping that grouped the line, so its copy joined every series into one zig-zag path. The copy now keeps the layer’s grouping (or its explicit group).

  • nudge_x / nudge_y follow the data axes, as in ggplot2 (VP-88): under coord_flip() nudge_y moves a label across and nudge_x up/down (they used to move it along the screen axes, so a flipped bar chart’s labels shifted by about one bar), and on a reversed axis a positive nudge points toward larger values. Applies to mark_text(), mark_label() and mark_image().

  • Bars, histograms, tiles and boxplot boxes draw on a reversed axis again (VP-89): scale_x_reverse() / scale_y_reverse(), with or without coord_flip(), drew no bars because their native width resolved to a negative size. Fixed in vellum (needs vellum with VP-89).

  • Bars on a continuous x axis are no longer clipped at the ends (VP-90). The x scale is now trained on each bar’s edges (centre +/- half its width, dodged groups included), not only its centre, as in ggplot2, so mark_bar(x = year, ...) gets a slightly wider x domain. Explicit limits, discrete and binned axes are unchanged. Histograms already trained on their bin edges.

  • A constant if_true in condition() is a setting, not a mapping (VP-86): alpha = condition("s", 1, 0.2) no longer adds an alpha legend titled “1” with keys 0.5-1.5. The same holds for colour, fill and size (color = condition("s", "red", "grey80") draws red points and no legend), and for a computed constant such as rgb(1, 0, 0). A mapped if_true still trains its scale and legend as before.

  • Date and date-time axes no longer overlap their labels (VP-92). The default breaks are chosen by the available width: pretty() breaks are thinned until the widest label, measured with vellum’s text metrics at the axis text size, fits between neighbouring ticks along an estimated axis length (75% of the plot’s width, or height for a vertical axis, shared among facet columns or rows). The default labels are now pretty()’s, as ggplot2 shows them: “2000”, “2002” for years, “Jan”, “Feb” for months, rather than full ISO dates. date_breaks, breaks and date_labels are used as given (date_labels is measured for the fit).

  • Effect underlays (glow(), outline(), shadow(), motion()) are keyed with their mark in animation keyframes (VR-34), so a halo fades in and out with its series or point instead of switching halfway and triggering the “cut rather than tween” warning.

  • With vellum’s morphing (VR-37), a line or area whose number of points changes between states morphs; animate()’s warning and docs no longer list it as something that switches (only lines that cannot be morphed do).

  • transition_reveal() with several series in one line, path, area, ribbon or step layer no longer draws a spike at the line end (VP-94): each series’ leading point is interpolated toward that series’ own next row (and within its facet panel), whatever the row order. The grouping lookup evaluated the wrong object and found no groups, so every series’ lead aimed at whichever row came next in along.

  • transition_reveal() reveals the data along along, as gganimate does (VP-81). It used to ignore along and wipe a clip across the panel left to right, background and gridlines included: a spiral wiped by x, a coord_flip() series wiped along the value axis and a reversed scale showed its newest data first. Each frame now shows the rows whose along has been reached – points appear as they are reached, and a line, path, area, ribbon or step grows through its rows with an interpolated leading point – on scales frozen over the whole data, with the background, grid, axes and legends drawn whole throughout. along may be numeric, Date or POSIXct. Each frame is its own keyframe, so animate() compiles nframes scenes (about 6 s for 100 frames of a 240-row time series).

  • animate() tweens marks by data identity, as gganimate matches by group (VR-32). Each mark is keyed by its data_id, else its group (or the combination of the layer’s discrete mapped aesthetics), then its order within that group; lines and areas by their group. Reordered or missing rows no longer blend unrelated marks into muddy colours, a bar race sorted by rank slides its bars between ranks in their own colours, and a colour group present in only one state fades in or out instead of cutting the whole transition. The cut warning now fires only for what truly cannot be matched (a line whose number of points changes). Needs vellum 0.13.0.9000.

  • animate() now warns, once, when adjacent states cannot tween mark for mark – a state that adds or drops a colour group, or a line whose number of points changes – naming the states. Such a transition now cuts to the next state halfway through instead of never showing it (VR-26, VR-27; the engine fix is in vellum). Needs vellum 0.13.0.9000.

  • transition_time() no longer drops a keyframe’s rows for integer times whose text form differs from the double’s, such as 100000L versus "1e+05" (VP-77).

  • animate(nframes =) must be a positive whole number; 2.5 used to be floored silently (VP-78).

  • Fractional fps (12.5, 0.5) is now written exactly instead of being rounded to a whole number (VL-15, in vellum).

  • Legends no longer list unused factor levels (VP-91). As in ggplot2, a discrete colour, fill, shape, linetype or pattern scale drops the levels no row uses, and the palette goes to the levels that remain (two used levels of four get the palette’s first two colours). A level used in only some facet panels stays. The discrete colour/fill scales (_discrete(), _manual(), _hue(), _brewer(), _viridis_d(), _grey(), _ordinal()), scale_shape(), scale_linetype() and their _manual() forms gain drop = FALSE to keep every level; limits still decide the levels.

Documentation

  • inst/examples/28-animation.R: part 2 now animates telephones by region (the same seven bars every year) so the bars visibly grow, and part 3 is a 12-phase wave with 10 frames per step, so every frame moves (VP-79). The animate(), ease_aes() and anim_save() examples use data with the same marks in every state, and animate() documents when states cut.

Tests

  • New mid-transition tests render the in-between frames for unequal counts, colour groups appearing and disappearing, changing vertex counts, changing text, two animated SVGs’ CSS isolation and fps timing (VP-80). The reordered-rows identity case (VR-32) is recorded as a skipped test.

vellumplot 0.18.1

Bug fixes

  • A line, path or step mapped to a continuous colour that holds constant within each series (mark_path(group = id, color = level) on contour lines) draws each series as one plain path in its colour. It used to draw one segment record per vertex pair: 91 volcano contours went from 9,097 records and 18.2k points to 91 records and 9.2k points. A series whose colour does vary is still coloured per segment (VP-76).

  • Two composition cells that condition the same aesthetic on the same selection (hconcat(p1, p2), each color = condition("s", ..., if_false)) no longer share a condition tag, so in vellumwidget each cell’s non-members take their own cell’s if_false, not the last cell’s. A tag that two cells share takes the cell id, "cell-<k>:<sel>:<aes>" (with any "@<layer>" suffix kept), in the elements and in interaction_model(); tags no other cell shares are unchanged (VP-75).

  • A per-row if_false of a color or fill condition (color = condition(sel, g, col)) is carried to the host as colours: a column of the scale’s levels (or numbers, on a continuous scale) is taken through that scale, as if_true is, and any other value is read as a colour (NA, the theme dim, when it is not one). It used to be the raw column, which a host could not paint. ?condition documents per-row if_false columns (VW-46).

vellumplot 0.18.0

  • Requires vellum (>= 0.13.0).

New features

  • An interactive mark_flow_map() keys its branches, so flows get hover, tooltips and selection in vellumwidget. A branch reaching a vertex the root has an edge to stands for that edge: it carries the edge’s two endpoints (the node keys, so select_neighbours() highlights a node’s flows), the edge’s key as join, and a key of its own (the edge key with a flow suffix) that never collides with the edge drawn by mark_edges(). A trunk merging several flows gets a key but no endpoints. The default tooltip names the root, the vertex the flow reaches and the flow; a layer tooltip replaces it. Faceted and composed plots prefix the keys and endpoints as they do for nodes and edges. A static render is unchanged (VP-71).

Bug fixes

  • Two layers that condition the same aesthetic on the same selection (a point layer and a text layer, each color = condition(sel, ..., if_false)) no longer share a condition tag. Each such layer’s elements and its interaction_model() condition carry "<sel>:<aes>@<layer>", so in vellumwidget a non-selected point takes its own layer’s if_false, not the text layer’s. Conditions also carry their tag in interaction_model(). Tags that no other layer shares stay "<sel>:<aes>" (VP-72).

  • Legend keys of filled marks now take the layer’s alpha, as ggplot2’s keys do. A mark_density() key draws its fill at the default alpha = 0.8 (VP-66) and keeps an outline opaque, as the curve does, and a set alpha on mark_density(), mark_area(), mark_ribbon(), mark_bar(), mark_histogram(), mark_tile(), mark_boxplot(), mark_violin() and the other filled marks reaches their keys. Before, the keys were opaque. A mapped alpha still draws its own legend and guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = )) still wins (VP-67).

  • Point and line legend keys now take a constant layer alpha too, as ggplot2’s draw_key_point() and draw_key_path() do: mark_point(color = g, alpha = 0.4) draws see-through colour keys, and so do the size, shape, line-type and line-width keys of a layer with a set alpha, a merged legend’s keys, and the keys of mark_edges(edge_alpha = ) and mark_nodes(alpha = ). Each key reads the layer that draws its glyph (a point layer for a point key). A mapped alpha still draws its own legend, override.aes still wins, and a mark_smooth() key stays opaque, since its alpha is the band’s and the fitted line is opaque (VP-70).

  • A mark_flow_map() in a graph faceted by a vertex attribute now draws, in each panel, only the edges whose two endpoints are both among the panel’s nodes, with those edges’ own weights, as mark_edges() has since VP-64. A panel without the root draws no flow. Before, every panel drew the whole flow map (VP-68).

vellumplot 0.17.1

  • Requires vellum (>= 0.12.0).

Performance

  • Faceting assigns rows to panels, and marks split rows into style groups, per distinct value instead of per row (VP-69): the level order, labels and panel rows are worked out once per facet value (or style tuple), and each panel’s rows come from one split() instead of a comparison over every row per panel. Building a 200,000-point scatter with facet_wrap() (4 panels) as a raster widget went from 1.46 s to 1.18 s. Scenes are unchanged.

  • Interactive marks carry their element meta (tooltips, legend membership, interval values, …) as columns, a data frame with one row per element, instead of a list with one record per element. vellum::scene_model() returns the same records as before, and vellumwidget reads the columns directly, so a large keyed plot no longer builds a record per point (VR-19). Needs vellum 0.11.1.9000 or later.

vellumplot 0.17.0

Behaviour changes

  • Behaviour change: an unmapped mark_area(), mark_ribbon(), mark_density(), mark_tile() or mark_raster() now fills with ggplot2’s default for areas, ribbons and tiles, col_mix(ink, paper, 0.2) from the theme’s element_geom(): "grey20" on a light theme, instead of "grey50". The old grey was the colour of theme_dark()’s panel, so a default area or density disappeared into it. Light-theme plots with these marks now draw them darker, matching ggplot2::layer_data() on theme_grey() and theme_dark(). ggplot2’s geom_density() is unfilled by default; mark_density() keeps its filled curve and fills it like an area (VP-60).

  • Behaviour change: mark_density() now draws its fill at alpha = 0.8 by default, so a single curve reads lighter than VP-60’s solid grey20 and overlapping groups (fill mapped) no longer hide the ones behind them. An alpha you set (including alpha = 1) or map still wins, and an outline (a color beside a fill) stays opaque. ggplot2’s geom_density() is unfilled, so there is no ggplot2 default to match here (VP-66).

  • Behaviour change: position = "jitterdodge" jitters as ggplot2’s position_jitterdodge() does: by default 40% of the resolution divided by (the most groups at any x + 2) each way, and not at all vertically. Before, it jittered 40% of the dodged slot sideways (0.15 instead of 0.1 of a category with two groups) and 40% of the y resolution up and down. A position_jitterdodge() built with the constructor already had no vertical jitter (VP-63).

Bug fixes

  • More of the colours vellumplot draws on its own now follow a dark theme’s element_geom() ink, paper and accent, as the mark defaults have since VP-58: legend keys for missing values (NA) and the pattern-key border, the nested size legend’s leader lines, vsparkline() (its line and bars col_mix(ink, paper, 0.3), its highlight dots and win bars the accent), including a sparkline added with annotate("sparkline"), vhierarchy() (cell borders and the root label; branch shades fade toward the paper), the vchord() ring borders and labels, mark_node_pie() wedge borders, leader lines to repelled labels, and the outline() effect, which now defaults to the paper colour. So theme_cyberpunk() no longer draws black chord labels on its black canvas. vsparkline(color, point_color, win_color), mark_node_pie(color) and outline(color) now default to NULL (the theme’s colour). Light themes draw exactly as before (VP-61).

  • Per-panel facet legends placed above or below the panels (a theme’s legend.position = "top" / "bottom") are now collected into one plot legend, with a message, when they would leave the panels shorter than 25 mm on the page. VP-59 did this only for legends beside the panels and only checked the panel width (VP-62).

  • A composition’s collected legend (guides = "collect") now goes where the composition theme’s legend.position puts it, as in patchwork: wrap_plots(a, b) |> theme(legend.position = "bottom") draws it in a row below the plots, spanning their panels. "left" and "top" work the same way, and "none" drops it. Before, it always went in a column on the right (VP-62).

  • position_dodge(preserve = "single") in a faceted plot now sizes every panel’s bars from the x with the most groups across the whole layer, as ggplot2 does. Before, each panel counted only its own groups, so a panel with at most two groups drew wider bars than one with three (VP-63).

  • A faceted interactive graph plot (vgraph() with facet_wrap()) keys each panel’s nodes and edges uniquely ("p1-2:v1"), with the vertex name as the cross-panel join. Before, edges repeated in every panel had the same keys. Edge endpoints now carry the same prefix as the node keys, also in compositions, where neighbour highlighting matched no node before (VP-63).

  • A graph plot faceted by a vertex attribute (vgraph() with facet_wrap() or facet_grid()) now draws in each panel only the edges whose two endpoints are both among that panel’s nodes, as ggraph’s facet_nodes() does. mark_edges(), mark_edge_text() and mark_edge_bundle() used to draw the whole edge table in every panel, with edges ending at nodes drawn in another panel. Each kept edge is now also capped at its own endpoints’ node sizes; before, a faceted panel looked them up by position and could cap an edge at another node’s radius. An edge keeps its key’s row number from the whole edge table, so its join is the same as in the unfaceted plot (VP-64).

  • On theme_dark(), mark_hex() with its count fill turned off (fill = NULL) and vwaffle()’s fallback cell fill no longer draw grey50 on the theme’s grey50 panel. When the default grey is that close to the panel, they fill with col_mix(ink, paper, 0.2) ("grey20"), the area fill. This differs from ggplot2, whose geom_hex() draws grey50 there. The colourbar and coloursteps frames now follow the theme’s ink and paper (theme_cyberpunk() draws them in its own mid grey). Light themes draw exactly as before (VP-65).

vellumplot 0.16.0

Behaviour changes

  • Behaviour change: position = "dodge" now splits the width at each x between the groups present there, as ggplot2’s position_dodge() does. Before, every x kept a slot for every group, so mark_bar(x = factor(cyl), fill = factor(gear), position = "dodge") left a gap for the missing gear-4 bar at cyl = 8; now that x shows two wider bars, centred. The default dodge width is now the bar width (90% of the band) instead of the whole band, so dodged bars touch, and a dodged box plot no longer leaves a gap between its boxes, both as in ggplot2. position_dodge(preserve = "single") keeps every element one group wide. Points now dodge with position = "dodge" too; before they were drawn undodged (VP-56).

  • Behaviour change: a discrete alpha, size or linewidth mapping now groups a layer too, as ggplot2 groups by every discrete aesthetic. Before, mark_line(x = wt, y = mpg, alpha = factor(am)) drew one line through all rows; now it draws one per am level, and stats (boxplots, densities, fits), stacks and dodges split the same way. mark_outlier_label() still judges outliers within colour / fill groups, so a discrete alpha or size there styles the labels without splitting the data (VP-57).

  • Behaviour change: default element keys (for an interactive layer that declares no data_id) now always name the panel, the layer and the row, as "p<row>-<col>:l<layer>:<row>": "p1-1:l2:7" is row 7 of layer 2 in the first (or only) panel. Composition cells keep their prefix in front ("subplot-2:p1-1:l1:7", "cell-1:p1-2:l1:7"). Before, keys were plain row numbers, so two default-keyed layers shared them: in mark_line(color = g) |> mark_point() |> select_point() selecting a point also selected the line whose first row had the same number. Keys made for a tooltip-only layer also repeated across facet panels. Both are fixed, and the "layer-<i>:" prefix from 0.15.0 is gone (VP-55). Layers no longer link through matching row numbers: to link elements on purpose, give the layers the same data_id = (for example data_id = g on both the line and the points). The same datum drawn in several facet panels or composition cells still links across them through its join id.

New features

  • Themes now set the default colours of unmapped marks, as ggplot2’s element_geom() does: theme(geom = element_geom(ink, paper, accent)). Points, lines, text and error bars use ink, bars and areas a mix of ink and paper, box plot, violin and label backgrounds paper, smooths and contours accent; element_geom(colour =, fill =) override them all. theme_cyberpunk() sets a light ink, so vplot(mtcars) |> mark_point(x = wt, y = mpg) |> theme_cyberpunk() no longer draws black points on its near-black panel, and legend keys of an unmapped colour follow suit. A theme_sketch() given its own ink / paper colours its marks with them. Light themes draw exactly as before; mapped scales and constant color = / fill = still win. mark_label()’s fill and the color / fill of mark_scalebar() / mark_compass() now default to the theme’s colours (white / black on light themes) (VP-58).

Bug fixes

  • In an aligned composition (wrap_plots(), |, /) each sub-plot’s legends now sit on the side their guide asks for (guide_legend(position = "bottom") and co.) or, failing that, where the sub-plot’s theme(legend.position = ) puts them: left, right, above or below its panel, or inside it. Before, every sub-plot legend went to a band on its right. Collected legends (guides = "collect") gather them from every side (VP-59).

  • Legends drawn beside each facet panel (guide_legend(position = "panel"), the default of an independent scale) are collected into the plot’s legend, titled "title (panel)", when they would leave the panels narrower than 25 mm on the page, with a message saying so. Before, a small page could squeeze the panels to slivers (VP-59).

vellumplot 0.15.1

  • annotate() layers no longer get default keys just because the plot declares a selection. A keyed annotation made the widget’s display list inexact, which switched off its zoomed canvas and detail tier for the whole plot (VW-24). An annotation with its own data_id or a condition() is still keyed.

  • Compiling a big plot is faster (VR-16): per-element legend membership, element meta records and SVG-marker lookup are built column-wise instead of with a closure per point. A 200k-point scatter compiles in about 0.65 s instead of 1.1 s. Output is unchanged.

vellumplot 0.15.0

Behaviour changes

  • Behaviour change: the legends of a scale resolved "independent" across facet panels (resolve_scale(color = "independent"), and size, alpha, shape, linetype, linewidth, pattern, fill) are now drawn beside each panel, titled with the scale title alone, instead of collected in the legend area as "title (panel)". guides(color = guide_legend(position = "right")) (or any other side) collects them as before. A panel with no values of an independent discrete scale no longer shows an empty legend (VP-53).

  • Behaviour change: a layer is now grouped by the interaction of all its discrete color, fill, pattern, linetype and shape mappings, as ggplot2 groups by every discrete aesthetic. Before, only the first of them formed the groups, so mark_bar(fill = gear, color = am) counted by am alone and dropped fill with a warning, and dodges, stacks and stats (densities, fits, boxplots) missed the other split. Now each (gear, am) pair is its own bar, box, curve or fit, ordered by the first aesthetic, then the next. mark_smooth() also draws a mapped linetype. A layer with a single discrete aesthetic (or one variable on several) groups as before (VP-52).

  • Behaviour change: scale_*_binned() now bins like ggplot2 by default (style = "extended"): about n “nice” class boundaries inside the data range, the outer classes widened to whole bins, classes closed on the right ((a, b]), and a colour-vector palette sampled at each class’s centre. Before, it cut the data at quantiles and spread the colours evenly; that is still style = "quantile". scale_*_steps() is now ggplot2’s two-colour binned scale (low, high, n.breaks, limits, …) rather than an alias of scale_*_binned(), and matches ggplot2’s breaks and colours (VP-49).

  • Behaviour change: scale_size_manual() and scale_alpha_manual() on a numeric variable now error, as in ggplot2 (“Continuous values supplied to a discrete scale”), instead of keying every distinct number (VP-49).

  • Behaviour change: color and fill are now separate scales, as in ggplot2. Each trains on its own channel’s values and draws its own legend; scale_fill_*() sets only the fill scale and scale_color_*() only the colour scale, so the two can be styled independently when both are mapped (before, both channels fed one pooled colour scale and the last scale declared won). The two legends merge into one when they show the same title and the same keys (one variable under one title), each key then filled by the fill scale and outlined by the colour scale; a colour bar and a fill bar of one variable fold into one bar when their palettes also match. In consequence: labs(fill =), guides(fill =), lims(fill =) and resolve_scale(fill =) address the fill scale only; a scale_fill_*() no longer recolours a color mapping (or the reverse); two layers mapping color and fill to variables of different type no longer clash; and a fill legend beside a separate colour legend tags its interactive keys "fill:<level>" (a lone fill legend keeps "color:<level>"). Plots that map only color or only fill render exactly as before (VP-48).

  • Behaviour change: mark_contour_filled() and mark_density_2d_filled() now draw ggplot2’s lowest band, from the highest break at or below the field’s minimum (0 for a density) to the first contour level, so the whole data grid is painted in the lowest colour as in geom_contour_filled(). Before, the region below the first level was left as panel background, and the fill scale started at the first level (VP-45).

New features

  • guide_legend(), guide_colourbar() / guide_colorbar(), guide_coloursteps(), guide_bins() and guide_bivariate() gain position = ("right", "left", "top", "bottom" or "inside"), as in ggplot2 3.5: it overrides theme(legend.position = ) for that legend only, so one plot can carry legends on several sides (VP-53).

  • The guide position "panel" draws a legend beside each facet panel: right of each panel by default, or on the side theme(legend.position = ) names (left, above, below, or inside each panel), justified along the panel edge by legend.justification. Each column (or row) of panels gets a legend track sized to its largest legend, for facet_wrap() and facet_grid(). Shared and per-panel legends mix in one plot (VP-53).

  • scale_*_stepsn() gains values =, the positions of its colours along the ramp, as in ggplot2 (VP-49).

  • bind_scale() is now enacted by vellumwidget: brushing an overview view zooms every view bound to the brush to the brushed range, and clearing the brush resets the zoom (overview + detail, Vega-Lite’s scale = list(domain = list(param = ...))). It now checks that it names an interval selection that constrains the bound axis (F-15).

  • select_interval() gains bind = "scales" (Vega-Lite’s bind: "scales"): the selection is the view’s own pan/zoom domain instead of a drawn brush, so zooming one view can drive bind_scale() on another (linked zoom) or a condition() / filter_by() (F-15).

  • Compositions (hconcat(), vconcat(), wrap_plots(), |, /) now give each cell’s panels a unique name ("cell-2-panel-1-1") and record the cell id in the panel meta. The panels of an aligned composition also carry the scale descriptors and pan group a single plot’s panel has, so a host can map their pixels to data and zoom them (axis-aware zoom, re-ticked axes). The interaction model tags each bind with its cell, and each selection with the cells that register it (F-15).

  • scale_x_date(), scale_x_datetime(), scale_x_time(), scale_x_binned() and their y counterparts take guide =, like the continuous and discrete position scales: scale_x_date(guide = guide_axis(n.dodge = 2)) staggers the month labels (VP-45).

  • spec_to_vegalite() exports free facet scales and resolve_scale() as the facet’s Vega-Lite resolve (resolve.scale, with resolve.axis for x / y and resolve.legend for the other aesthetics), and spec_from_vegalite() reads a facet-level resolve.scale back. Before, the exporter ignored resolution, so free scales came out shared (VP-47).

  • guide_bins() draws the legend of a binned scale as ggplot2’s does: one key per bin, edge to edge, with the bin boundaries (not interval labels) on a small axis beside them; show.limits = TRUE also labels the outer limits. It works on scale_size_binned(), scale_alpha_binned() and the binned colour scales, vertically and in a top / bottom legend (VP-45).

Bug fixes

  • Default element keys no longer coincide with user data_ids. A mark keyed by default (row position, or a line’s first row) got keys such as "1", so in mark_line(x = t, y = v) |> mark_point(x = t, y = v, data_id = t) the line and the point with t = 1 shared a key and were selected together. In a plot where any layer declares a data_id, default keys now carry their layer ("layer-1:1"); user data_ids, and the keys of plots without one, are unchanged (VP-54).

  • An aligned composition (hconcat(), vconcat(), wrap_plots() of single-panel plots) now keeps the theme’s plot.margin around the figure, as a single plot does. Before, the first row’s panels touched the top edge and the last column’s the right edge (VP-50).

  • Element keys no longer collide between the cells of a composition when a cell is faceted (or otherwise drawn as a whole plot rather than aligned). Such a cell names its panels panel-r-c like a lone plot, so two faceted cells both keyed marks "panel-1-1:3" and hovering or brushing one cell lit up the other. Their keys now start with the cell id ("cell-2:panel-1-1:3"), with the unprefixed row kept as the join id, as aligned cells’ keys start with subplot-N. Lone plots are unchanged (VP-51).

  • ggplot2 plots no longer break when vellumplot is attached after ggplot2. ggplot2 looks default scales (scale_colour_continuous(), …) and guides given by name (guide = "legend") up along the search path, where it found vellumplot’s constructors of the same name. Those constructors now hand a call coming from ggplot2 back to ggplot2’s own (VP-49).

  • A merged legend (colour + shape, size, alpha, …) of a filled mark now draws the mark’s constant outline or fill in its keys, as a lone colour legend has since 0.14.0 (VP-48).

  • scale_fill_identity() declared a colour scale instead of a fill scale (VP-48).

  • guide_axis(check.overlap = TRUE) now also thins the labels of free facet scales (panel by panel), fixed-aspect plots (coord_fixed(), coord_sf(), aspect.ratio) and marginal plots; before, it silently kept every label there. Polar axes still keep every label (VP-45).

  • position_dodge() / position_dodge2() on a horizontal mark_errorbar(), mark_linerange() or mark_pointrange() (orientation = "y") now dodge the groups along y, the category axis, as a horizontal box plot does and as in ggplot2. Before, horizontal error bars were not dodged at all and a horizontal point-range’s points were shifted along the value axis (VP-45).

vellumplot 0.14.1

Bug fixes

  • add_marginal(group = TRUE) fills each group’s histogram or density in its colour again. Since 0.14.0 made a color given with a fill an outline (VP-46), the marginals’ constant grey fill turned the group colours into thin outlines on grey.

vellumplot 0.14.0

Behaviour changes

  • Behaviour change: a discrete colour scale now honours character limits (e.g. lims(color = c("a", "b"))): it covers just those levels, in that order, and other levels draw in the NA colour. Before, the limits of a discrete colour scale were ignored. Legend labels on a discrete colour scale may now be a function of the levels or a vector named by level (VP-43).

  • Behaviour change: rows a position scale’s oob = "censor" puts outside its limits are now counted in the “Removed n rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range (layer k, mark_x())” warning instead of vanishing silently, and – for the marks that draw one element per row, including boxplot, violin and smooth – they are removed before the layer’s statistic, as in ggplot2 (VP-41).

  • Behaviour change: on the filled marks a color given alongside a fill now outlines the shapes instead of overriding the fill, as in ggplot2: mark_histogram(fill = "#3182bd", color = "white") draws blue bars with white edges, where it used to draw white bars. This covers mark_bar(), mark_histogram(), mark_count(), mark_area(), mark_density() (top edge only), mark_ribbon() (both edges), mark_tile(), mark_bin2d(), mark_hex(), mark_crossbar() (box and middle line), mark_dotplot(), mark_pie() and mark_donut(), matching mark_rect() and mark_polygon(); the slab of mark_halfeye() takes the fill and leaves color to the point-interval. A mapped color beside a constant fill outlines in the mapped colours. A lone color still fills, as before. Legend keys draw the constant outline (or the constant fill inside an outlined box) too, also for box plots, violins and ridgelines (VP-46).

New features

  • More ggplot2 scale constructors, with ggplot2’s argument names (VP-43): scale_shape_manual(), scale_linetype_manual(), scale_size_manual() and scale_alpha_manual() (with breaks, labels, limits and na.value; shape and line-type values also take ggplot2’s numeric codes); scale_*_hue(), scale_*_grey() and scale_*_ordinal(); the binned scale_*_steps2(), scale_*_stepsn(), scale_*_fermenter() and scale_*_viridis_b(), which bin with ggplot2’s breaks (nice boundaries, right-closed classes) and take oob; scale_size_binned(), scale_radius(), scale_size_continuous(), scale_size_discrete() / scale_size_ordinal(), scale_alpha_discrete() / scale_alpha_ordinal(), scale_shape_discrete(); and the position shortcuts scale_x_log10(), scale_x_sqrt(), scale_x_reverse() and their y forms. Each colour scale also has its color and fill spellings. scale_*_manual() for colour gains breaks, labels, limits and na.value, and scale_shape() / scale_linetype() gain breaks, labels, limits and na.value.

  • New guide_axis() for the position axes, used as guides(x = ) / guides(y = ) or the new guide argument of scale_x_continuous(), scale_y_continuous(), scale_x_discrete() and scale_y_discrete(): n.dodge staggers crowded labels over rows (or columns), angle rotates them, check.overlap drops labels that would collide, minor.ticks adds minor ticks and cap ends the axis line at the outermost breaks. The label gutter is measured with the dodging and rotation, so nothing clips. guides(x = "none") draws an axis without labels or ticks. guide_axis_logticks() draws long, middle and short log10 ticks (F-17).

  • mark_halfeye() and mark_interval() gain orientation, inferred as for box plots and violins: a discrete y with a continuous x draws horizontal intervals, with the slab above each one (VP-42).

  • scale_*_gradient(), scale_*_gradient2(), scale_*_gradientn(), scale_*_viridis_c() and scale_*_distiller() gain limits, oob and na.value (and the gradients breaks / labels), as scale_*_continuous() has; the default oob = NULL keeps today’s behaviour (VP-41).

  • mark_density_2d() and mark_density_2d_filled(): 2-D kernel density contours with ggplot2’s geom_density_2d() semantics (h, adjust, contour_var, one estimate per group); mark_quantile() draws quantile regression lines like geom_quantile() (needs quantreg); mark_errorbar(), mark_linerange() and mark_pointrange() gain orientation and draw horizontally when given xmin/xmax but no ymin/ymax, like geom_errorbarh() (F-16).

  • New geometry marks matching ggplot2’s (F-16): mark_rect() (corner bounds, now a documented layer mark rather than only annotate("rect"); color outlines alongside a fill), mark_polygon() (one polygon per group, holes via subgroup), mark_path() (connects rows in data order), mark_curve() (curvature, angle, ncp) and mark_spoke() (angle + radius).

  • Independent non-position scales across facet panels: resolve_scale() now accepts color (colour, fill), size, alpha, shape, linetype, linewidth, pattern and the edge scales. "independent" trains that scale in each panel from the panel’s own data, and each panel gets its own legend, collected in the legend area and titled with the scale title and the panel’s strip text ("hp (cyl: 4)"). Shared scales keep their single legend, and the default (everything shared) is unchanged (F-8).

Bug fixes

  • Wrapped x tick labels reserve the height of the label that wraps to the most lines, not of the longest one, so a short-worded label no longer runs into the axis title (F-17).

  • In a composition (|, /, wrap_plots()), each sub-plot now honours its own theme(legend.position = "inside") (or c(x, y)), drawing its legend over its panel instead of in a right-hand band, and legend.position = "none" hides that sub-plot’s legend. With guides = "collect" only the legends placed outside their panels are collected (VP-41).

  • Filled contour bands (mark_contour_filled(), mark_density_2d_filled()) no longer flood the panel when a band spans two peaks: every band now closes along the edge of the density grid. Groups with too few points for a 2-D density (e.g. in a facet panel holding other groups) are skipped instead of failing the plot (F-16).

  • A literal xend, yend, xmin, xmax, ymin or ymax (e.g. mark_segment(xend = 5)) is a coordinate again: it trains its axis and is drawn, rather than being taken for a constant style setting (F-16).

  • as_spec() (and spec_to_json()) serialize a facet’s declarative labeller: label_value, label_both, label_wrap_gen(width), a named character vector, and as_labeller() over a lookup table with one of those as its default. They round-trip through from_spec() / spec_from_json() and render the same strips. Only an arbitrary labeller function still raises the classed vellumplot_unserializable error (VP-44).

vellumplot 0.13.0

Behaviour changes

  • Behaviour change: a discrete colour scale (scale_*_manual(), scale_*_discrete(), scale_*_brewer(), …) on a numeric variable now errors (“Continuous values supplied to a discrete colour scale”), as in ggplot2, instead of giving every distinct number its own colour (VP-11).

  • Behaviour change: discrete position axes drop factor levels no row uses, as ggplot2 does by default; scale_x_discrete(drop = FALSE) keeps them (F-10).

  • Behaviour change: x = Inf / -Inf (and y) on a continuous axis now sits on the panel edge, as in ggplot2, rather than being lost (VP-11).

  • Behaviour change: a factor, character or logical mapped to size or alpha now trains a discrete scale, as in ggplot2. Before, a factor was trained as its integer codes (the legend read 1.0, 1.5, … 3.0, never merged with a colour legend of the same variable, and the marks failed to draw) and a character failed outright. The levels now spread evenly over the output range (by area for size), the legend keys are the levels, and a discrete size or alpha legend merges with a colour or shape legend of the same title and levels (#220). As in ggplot2, an unordered variable warns that size or alpha “for a discrete variable is not advised”; an ordered factor does not. scale_size() and scale_alpha() breaks pick the levels the legend shows, and range sets the spread (VP-39).

  • Behaviour change: guide_coloursteps() labels each bin boundary on its own, in the colourbar’s plain number style, so quantile breaks that span orders of magnitude read 0.0002, 0.066, 2.32, 193, 806 instead of all padded to the smallest one’s precision (0.0002 ... 806.0000) (VP-33).

  • Behaviour change: the grammar lint rules (single_level_scale, legend_overflow) now check discrete shape, linetype and pattern scales as well as colour ones. They were meant to all along, but only a colour scale reported itself as discrete, so a one-level shape went unflagged. guide_legend(reverse = TRUE) now also reverses a pattern legend (R-14).

  • Stacks follow the group key, whatever aesthetic defines it (VP-38). Without group, color or fill, a discrete pattern, linetype or shape now groups the layer. Behaviour change: mark_bar(pattern = category, position = "stack") now stacks in legend order (first level on top), as stacks grouped by fill have since the stack order change above. Before, a pattern-only layer was one group, so its stack ran in data order. Stats and dodges group by such an aesthetic too, as in ggplot2 (for example mark_density(linetype = g) draws one curve per g).

  • A violin or ridgeline fill that varies within a shape is dropped with a warning (VP-37). Each violin (ridge, slab) is one polygon with one fill, so mark_violin(fill = <continuous>) painted every shape with its first row’s fill while the legend showed a gradient. As in ggplot2, whose violins are computed by a stat that drops such aesthetics, the varying fill (or color, alpha, …) is now dropped with a warning, and no legend is drawn for it. A continuous fill that is constant within each category is kept. (Areas and ribbons error instead, as ggplot2’s do.)

  • Stat edge cases follow ggplot2 (VP-22).

    • Behaviour change: a stat layer with too few points (a density of one value, a smooth through one x, a hull of two points) or no finite values now warns and draws nothing, whether or not it is grouped. Before, an ungrouped layer aborted the whole plot while a grouped one only warned.
    • A plot whose data has zero rows draws an empty panel instead of reporting that it “needs an x and y encoding”. A plot that really maps no x (or no y) now says which axis is missing.
    • mark_rug(x = ) (or y =) works on its own, with a blank axis for the unmapped direction.
    • The numeric stats (histogram, density, smooth, …) warn “Removed n rows containing non-finite values” for rows they leave out because an input is Inf or missing, as ggplot2’s stats do, instead of dropping them silently.

  • Small stat differences from ggplot2 are fixed (VP-23).

    • Behaviour change: mark_count()’s after_stat(prop) is the share of the point’s group, so each colour’s bubbles sum to 1 (ggplot2’s stat_sum()). Before, it was the share of the whole layer.
    • The count stat behind mark_bar() now names its proportion prop, as ggplot2 does. after_stat(density) still works as an alias.
    • Behaviour change: mark_density() evaluates the curve over the range of the layer’s data, as ggplot2 does, instead of running on ~3 bandwidths past it. The x axis is no longer padded by the kernel’s tails, and every group’s curve spans the same x. The new trim = TRUE ends each group’s curve at its own data.
    • Behaviour change: mark_violin() trims each violin to the range of its data by default, as ggplot2’s geom_violin() does. Use trim = FALSE for the old untrimmed outline.
    • Behaviour change: mark_hull(expand =) and mark_node_hull(expand =) grow each hull by a uniform margin with rounded corners, a fraction of the layer’s range on each axis, instead of scaling it about its centroid. A long thin hull now gets the same margin as a round one, and every hull in a layer gets the same margin whatever its size. mark_node_hull()’s default expand is now 0.04.

New features

  • mark_histogram() bins like ggplot2. It gains binwidth, breaks, boundary, center and closed, with ggplot2’s meaning: breaks gives the bin edges (bins may differ in width), binwidth the width, and boundary / center where the bins are aligned. The bin stat also computes ncount and ndensity, and the x axis now covers the outer bars’ edges (F-10).

    Behaviour change: the default bins = 30 now places bins as ggplot2 does, with the outer bins centred on the smallest and largest values (width range / (bins - 1)), instead of 30 bins from the minimum to the maximum. Counts now match geom_histogram() for the same bins.

  • New mark_freqpoly() draws the bin counts as a frequency polygon, one line per group, padded with an empty bin at each end like ggplot2’s geom_freqpoly(). It takes the same binning arguments as mark_histogram() (F-10).

  • mark_summary() draws ranges. With fun.data ("mean_se", "mean_cl_normal", "mean_sdl", "median_hilow", or a function such as ggplot2::mean_se()), or with fun.min / fun.max, it summarises each category into a point and a range and draws a point range, like ggplot2’s stat_summary(). fun.args passes extra arguments. Without them it draws points as before (F-10).

  • Horizontal box plots and violins. mark_boxplot() and mark_violin() gain orientation. By default it is inferred as in ggplot2: a discrete y with a continuous x (mark_boxplot(x = mpg, y = factor(cyl))) draws horizontal boxes / violins, and the axis is widened for the violin outline as for vertical ones. orientation = "x" or "y" forces either (F-10).

  • facet_wrap() and facet_grid() take a labeller argument for the strip text, with ggplot2’s labellers: label_value(), label_both() ("cyl: 4"), label_wrap_gen(width) for long values, and as_labeller() for a lookup table (c("0" = "automatic")) or a function of the values. A named character vector or a plain function can be passed to labeller = directly. With several facet variables a strip shows one line per variable, centred, and the strip grows to fit (F-10).

  • guide_bivariate() labels the swatch edges with the class breaks bi_class() chose, along both axes, so the legend says which range each colour stands for (labels = FALSE turns them off; the swatches widen to fit them unless key.size is set). guide_bivariate(rotate = TRUE) turns the grid 45 degrees into a diamond, low-low at the bottom and high-high at the top. The “Scales and guides” article has a new bivariate section (VP-35).

  • scale_x_discrete() / scale_y_discrete() gain breaks (the levels that get a tick), labels (a vector, a vector named by level, or a function) and drop (F-10).

  • scale_x_continuous(), scale_y_continuous(), scale_color_continuous(), scale_fill_continuous(), scale_size() and scale_alpha() gain oob: "censor", "squish", "keep" or a function(x, range) such as scales::oob_squish_any(), with scales::oob_*() semantics. The defaults are unchanged: positions and sizes keep out-of-limits values, colours squish them (F-10).

  • Legends can sit inside the panels: theme(legend.position = "inside") with legend.position.inside = c(x, y) and legend.justification, or the older legend.position = c(x, y). Positions are fractions of the panel area; the justification (a c(x, y) or words such as c("right", "top")) defaults to the position, so c(1, 1) tucks the legend into the top-right corner (F-10).

  • coord_cartesian(xlim =, ylim =) (and the other coords’ limits) now zoom a discrete axis too, in level positions as in ggplot2: xlim = c(2, 4) shows the second to fourth levels (VP-11).

  • spec_diagnose()’s $report now also counts the rows a stat leaves out itself, in a new stat column: an infinite value in a histogram, density, smooth or 2-D bin, or every row of a group too small for a density, smooth, ellipse or hull. The stats record which input rows they skip, and the report maps those back to the layer’s data across facet panels, so the count matches what the compile draws. Limits now follow each scale’s oob: a clipped or censored position, or a censored size, counts under limits. A second new column, oob, counts rows that are outside a scale’s limits but still drawn (a squished position, or a colour, fill, size, alpha or linewidth value that is clamped, given the NA colour or extrapolated). Those rows are not part of dropped, and each layer with any adds its own warning. The pre-compile check for a manual or discrete colour palette on a continuous variable is now an error, matching the compile, which refuses it (VP-36, #208).

  • Stat parameters are checked where you write them. bins, binwidth, adjust, span, level, height, segments and n in mark_histogram(), mark_hex(), mark_bin2d(), mark_dotplot(), mark_density(), mark_violin(), mark_ridgeline(), mark_halfeye(), mark_smooth(), mark_ellipse() and mark_contour() are validated by the constructor, with an error naming the argument. Before, bins = 0 crashed with “arguments imply differing number of rows”, adjust = 0 with “‘bw’ is not positive”, and level = 2 or binwidth = -1 drew a wrong plot without complaint (VP-21).

Bug fixes

  • Violins on a binned axis keep their shape (VP-30). With scale_y_binned(), a violin’s density (and the axis room made for it) was estimated from the values snapped to their bin centres, giving a lumpy outline cut off at the outer centres. The density now uses the continuous values.

  • An aesthetic whose values are all missing no longer draws a 0-1 colourbar or size legend; a continuous scale with no data and no limits draws no legend (VP-11).

  • A two-vertex graph on the default stress layout no longer warns “data length [3] is not a sub-multiple or multiple of the number of rows [2]”. The warning came from graphlayouts’ fixed two-vertex branch; vgraph() now returns that same layout itself (VP-40).

  • Faceted interactive plots without a data_id no longer link marks across panels by accident. Their default element keys were row positions within each panel’s layer, so they repeated from panel to panel, and a hover, click or brush in one panel also lit up the marks at the same positions in the others. Default keys in a faceted plot are now "<panel>:<row>", using the source row when the layer draws one element per input row, and that source row is carried as the element’s join id so a declarative selection still matches the same datum wherever it is drawn. Single-panel plots and declared data_ids are unchanged (VW-11).

  • md(), vl_pattern(), sketch(), linear_gradient() and radial_gradient() are now vellum’s own functions re-exported, not wrappers around them. They behave the same, but attaching vellum and vellumplot together (as library(vellumverse) does) no longer reports them as conflicts. pdf_pages() and render_all() differ from vellum’s (they take plots, and pdf_pages() splits a faceted plot into pages), so they stay, and their docs now say how they differ (VV-2).

Internal

  • Internal: a trained scale now records its scale type (continuous, discrete, binned, identity, …) in type for every aesthetic, where kind held the type for colour and position scales and the aesthetic name for the rest. The provenance scale-refs report the same type values as before (R-14).

vellumplot 0.12.0

New features

  • select_interval() brushes a data range. select_interval(name, encodings = "x") declares an interval selection that a brush fills; condition() and filter_by() react to it the same way they react to a point selection. Membership is by data value: a host such as vellumwidget converts the brushed pixels to a data range through the panel’s scale and tests each element’s own values, so continuous (including log, sqrt and reversed), date, datetime and discrete axes all work, and a brush in one facet selects matching rows in every facet. encodings takes "x", "y" or c("x", "y"). Plots with an interval selection now carry each keyed element’s data values on the brushed channels, and the panel axis descriptors gain aesthetic and, for discrete axes, levels. The interaction model records the selection as {name, type: "interval", encodings}. Static renders are unchanged.

    encodings defaults to c("x", "y"), the same rectangle brush as before. The old on = "x" / "y" / "xy" argument still works as an alias.

  • Bivariate choropleths with a 2-D legend. bi_class() bins two numeric columns into dim classes each (quantile by default, or any scale_fill_binned() style) and adds one "x-y" class column. Mapping a fill or colour to that column colours it from a bivariate palette and draws the legend as a square grid of swatches, with the x variable along the bottom, the y variable up the side, and an arrow on each axis. scale_fill_bivariate() / scale_color_bivariate() choose the palette (bi_pal(): Stevens’ "DkBlue", "GrPink", "DkViolet" and "Brown", at 2x2, 3x3 or 4x4) and the axis titles, and guide_bivariate() retitles the axes or resizes the swatches through guides(). It works on mark_sf() polygons and on ordinary marks. The classes are computed over the whole table, so facet panels share them. On an interactive plot each swatch is keyed to the features in its class, so hovering a swatch highlights them.

  • A mapped linewidth tapers smoothly along the line (#165). mark_line() and mark_step() drew a mapped linewidth as one segment per span, each at the mean of its two endpoint widths, so the width jumped at every vertex and every series became a batch of separate path elements. Each series is now one lines_grob(lwd_profile =) stroke from vellum whose width varies linearly between the values at its vertices, so the taper is continuous and the series is a single element in vellum::scene_model(), vellum::element_geometry() and the SVG, keyed like a constant-width line. A series falls back to the old per-segment drawing where a tapered stroke cannot express it: a continuous colour (each segment keeps its own colour), a dashed or dotted linetype, a sketch theme, or a missing width.

  • spec_diagnose() reports rows that will not be shown and catches spec mistakes before compiling. vellumplot never deletes rows, so a row with a missing position, a value of zero or less on a log axis, or a value outside explicit scale limits used to disappear without a word. spec_diagnose() now also takes a PlotSpec, and its result carries a report data frame with one row per layer counting those rows by reason (missing, facet, transform, limits). Each layer that loses rows adds a warning. Three checks now run before the dry-run compile: a facet variable missing from the plot data (an error) or from a layer’s own data (a warning, since that layer repeats in every panel); color and fill mapped to a continuous and a discrete variable although they share one legend (a named error in place of the generic compile failure); and a manual or discrete palette on a continuous colour channel, which turns every distinct number into its own category. The result now prints as a short summary.

Bug fixes

  • Date axes take their breaks from the limits. Default date and datetime breaks were picked from the data, so a month of data under limits of 2019 to 2022 crammed weekly ticks into that month and left the rest of the axis bare. Breaks now span the trained range, limits included. An all-NA Date column no longer aborts with “‘from’ must be a finite number”; the axis draws with no ticks, as in ggplot2 (VP-8).

  • Theme text sizes cascade from text. theme(text = element_text(size = 20)) resized only the axis titles; axis text, legend text, strips and the plot title kept their own fixed sizes. The complete themes now size every text element relative to the text root, so the change reaches all of them. New rel() gives a size as a multiple of the inherited one (theme(axis.text = element_text(size = rel(0.8)))), and every complete theme takes base_size and base_family, as in ggplot2. Default sizes are unchanged. Colours set by a preset (grey axis text, for example) still win over a text colour, as in ggplot2 (VP-10).

  • A layer’s own data is faceted on the variables it has. In facet_grid(am ~ cyl), an annotation layer whose data had am but not cyl was drawn in all six panels. It now appears only in its am row, repeated across the cyl columns, as in ggplot2. A layer without any facet variable is still drawn in every panel. Facet levels are now the union over the plot data and every layer’s data, so a level that only a layer has gets its own panel instead of being dropped. The spec_diagnose() warning for a missing facet variable now says which panels the layer is repeated in (VP-9).

  • mark_rule() draws each rule in its own colour. A mapped color, alpha or linetype used to collapse to the first row, so every rule took one colour while the legend showed several. The rules are now split into style groups, as mark_abline() styles each line.

  • Repelled labels survive missing values. mark_text(repel = TRUE) and mark_label(repel = TRUE) crashed when any row had an NA position or label: the solver skips such labels, so its solution had fewer rows than the label grob and the offsets were recycled to the wrong length. Incomplete rows are now dropped before the labels are drawn, and the solved offsets are applied by element index.

  • Missing values are shown or reported, never dropped silently. They now follow ggplot2 (VP-6):

    • A missing category on a discrete position is a trailing "NA" level, so its rows are drawn and mark_bar() counts them as an NA bar. Before, sort() dropped the level and the rows were emitted at NaN. Explicit discrete limits still decide what is shown. Colour, shape and the other discrete scales already drew NA in their na_value with an “NA” legend key, and still do.
    • A missing facet value gets its own trailing "NA" panel (last on each dimension of a grid). Before, its rows vanished: facet_wrap(~cyl) on data with three missing cyl values drew 29 of 32 rows.
    • A row missing a continuous position (x, y, xend, ymin, …) is removed before the stat, with one warning per layer, “Removed n rows containing missing values”. Provenance no longer lists it as drawn. Lines, steps, areas and ribbons keep such rows as a gap, as before.
    • spec_diagnose() counts exactly those removed rows as missing. Its report loses the facet column, since a missing facet value is now drawn, and it no longer repeats the compile warning.

  • An inset plot no longer resets the outer plot’s interaction context. A sub-plot drawn inside a plot (annotate("sparkline"), or annotate("grob") with a plot) set the shared mark context for itself and left it that way, so the outer plot’s later panels lost their selection keys, filter_by() tags and page size. Each plot now saves the context it was called with and restores it when it returns (VP-12).

  • position_stack() and position_fill() stack like ggplot2. Positive and negative heights now stack separately, away from zero, so y = c(2, -1, 3) at one x no longer draws overlapping spans. Every row at an x stacks, so bars or areas with no fill/group mapped pile up instead of all starting at zero. Grouped areas sampled at different x values are interpolated onto the union of their x values (as ggplot2’s stat_align() does) and stack; before, they were never stacked and overlapped. Under position_fill() the negative stack fills [-1, 0].

    Behaviour change: the stack order is reversed to match ggplot2. The first group level now sits on top and the last at the bottom, so the stack reads in the same order as the legend. Plots that relied on the old bottom-up order (including pie slices built from a stacked bar) draw their segments in the opposite order. A stacked label with vjust = 1 on a negative bar now sits at its far (lower) end, as in ggplot2.

  • Legends merge on title and keys, as in ggplot2. A colour and a size legend merged whenever their titles matched, so two variables under one labs() title drew one legend with the size keys painted in the wrong colours. Meanwhile colour and linetype mapped to the same variable drew two legends. Legends now merge only when they share the title and the same keys and labels, and any pair of keyed legends can merge: colour, shape, linetype, size, alpha and linewidth. A merged key draws a line when a linetype or line width is involved, a point for shape or size, or both (VP-7).

  • Provenance carries every trained scale. plot_provenance() records listed scale-refs only for x, y, colour/fill, size and shape. A mapped alpha, linetype, linewidth or pattern now carries its scale-ref too, as do the edge colour, alpha and linetype channels of a graph. linewidth names the line-width scale on a line, step or segment and the edge-width scale elsewhere. The aesthetics that the scale trainer, the legend builder and provenance each listed separately now come from one internal registry.

  • Alt text names the drawn axes under coord_flip(). The automatic description said “It plots y (vertical axis) against x (horizontal axis)” even when coord_flip() drew x up the side. It now names the scale on each drawn axis, including the implicit “count” axis of a flipped bar chart. The description also follows a labs() alias the legend already honoured, so labs(fill = "Cylinders") on a fill mapping is “colour shows Cylinders” rather than the mapped expression. Axes, legends, alt text and the lint summary now read one titles record computed once per panel build, so they can no longer disagree about a title (VP-11).

vellumplot 0.11.1

Bug fixes

  • Violins, ridgelines and half-eyes draw cleanly on log and sqrt axes. The density was estimated on the raw data and its support, which stats::density() pads by about three bandwidths, was then mapped through the scale. For data near zero that padding dips to or below zero, so a log10 or sqrt axis produced NaN outline vertices. The density is now estimated on the transformed values, as ggplot2 does, so every vertex is finite and the trained axis still covers the drawn shape. On a transformed axis the shape is now the density of the transformed values; identity axes draw exactly as before.

  • A widened density axis gets ticks over its tails. The axis is widened to fit a violin’s or ridgeline’s tails, but the breaks had already been picked for the raw data range, so the tails ran past the last labelled tick. The breaks are now re-picked over the widened extent. Breaks you set yourself are left alone.

  • Tooltips and data keys follow stats that reorder or summarise rows. tooltip, data_id, hover_group, hover_color and selected_color were still in pre-stat row order after a stat. A dot plot sorts its dots, so each dot showed another row’s tooltip and key. A bin2d or hex layer that happened to have as many cells as input rows keyed every cell with an unrelated row. These values now go through the same realignment as aesthetics. A row-preserving stat (dot plot, outlier label, window, series label, count) gives each element its own row’s value. A summarising stat (bin, bin2d, hex, density, smooth, …) keeps a value only if it is constant within each group (tooltip = species on a per-species density) or across the whole layer. Otherwise the value is dropped, because a summary element has no single row to take it from.
